title: Retention beyond the paywall: the 2:1 lifecycle email strategy for apps
summary: Jake argues app founders stop marketing the moment someone downloads, leaving users with only billing emails. He recommends fixing the product first, then running a simple 2:1 email cadence (two value emails, one offer) plus a winback system for lapsed users.

principles.text: Use 15% annual retention as the working benchmark for consumer apps, so plan for churn and non-renewal.
principles.quote: For consumer apps, a 15% annual retention should be your working benchmark.

principles.text: Most apps have no system for winning back or keeping customers, then overspend on acquisition just to hold MRR flat.
principles.quote: But after consulting on over 100 apps, most have no system for winning back customers or preventing them from leaving in the first place.

principles.text: Email can't save a weak product. Find what retained users repeat and make that feature faster and more valuable.
principles.quote: Look at the behaviors retained users repeat, find the feature they use most, then make that experience faster, easier and more valuable.

principles.text: Start lifecycle email with a 2:1 ratio: two value emails for every one offer-based email.
principles.quote: a 2:1 ratio strategy is what I usually recommend to start with: Two emails that add value, One email that is offer based

principles.text: Monetization doesn't end at the first paywall. Existing users who understand the product are the best audience for the next relevant offer or upsell.
principles.quote: a customer who already understands your product is often the most logical person to show the next useful offer.

principles.text: Lapsed users often didn't hate the product, so a useful email lets you re-enter the conversation without re-buying their attention.
principles.quote: A useful email gives you a chance to re-enter the conversation without buying that person's attention all over again.
